newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPC eyes 70 pct Hagenuk stake, paper says.
newsitem.headline: IPC eyes 70 pct Hagenuk stake, paper says.

text.p: Singapore computer maker IPC Corp is in talks with German telecommunications equipment firm Hagenuk Telecom GmbH to raise its stake in the company to about 70 percent, the daily Straits Times (ST) said on Friday.

"It is likely to be in the region of 70 percent," ST quoted a source as saying. "I can't give an exact figure now because things are at a very sensitive stage but it certainly won't be anything less than 70 percent, I can tell you that."

The paper said the increase in stake was expected to take place in the next few weeks and would require IPC to invest at least another Singapore $50 million, bringing its total investment to about S$100 million.
It said the new investment was likely to be via subscription to a new issue of Hagenuk shares as well through the purchase of existing shares from other shareholders.

The other shareholders of Hagenuk are Manfred Schmitt, founder of German personal computer retailer Escom who holds a 37.5 percent stake and London-based venture capital company 3i with 12.7 percent stake.
Hong Kong's Keeneast and Malaysian contract manufacturer Tru-Tech both have minor shares.
IPC's chairman Patrick Ngiam said in March that Hagenuk was planning to list in the United States or on one of Europe's markets within the next 12 months.
